text:
jamie: Heads-up — prod console alerts: heatmap route LCP spike in us-west after yesterday's bundle commit. 95th went from ~130ms -> ~460ms.
oana: saw that too. any correlation with the bundle-size bump from the analytics lib merge?
jamie: yes — build diff shows +320KB gzipped for shared-visuals. looks like we accidentally inlined a heavy dependency into shared-chunk.
rui: that matches traces: main-thread time dominated by parse/eval of shared-visuals at cold load. also seeing more kvcache lookups.
taylor: is it just parsing cost or are we hitting more network roundtrips?
jamie: combo: parse/eval + kvcache prefix misses. splitpoint routing change last week routed more heatmap requests to the eu pool for affinity testing, which increased cross-region tile fetch latency for some clients.
oana: oh yeah the routing policy change set heatmap to prefer region-affinity=best-effort, not strict. that explains random cross-region fetches.
rui: telemetry snippets: 
- shared-visuals parse median: 38ms -> 160ms (cold)
- kvcache miss-rate on heatmap-route: 0.6% -> 3.4%
- cross-region tile latency p95: 90ms -> 210ms

taylor: ouch. any quick mitigations?
jamie: short-term: 1) rollback the shared-visuals change or 2) ship an emergency canary that keeps the new break but forces heatmap splitpoint to inline priority. which is less risky?
oana: rollback simpler and faster. downside: loses other benefits from analytics lib update.
rui: we can also flip routing policy back to strict region affinity for heatmap routes while we investigate. that avoids rollback and reduces cross-region latency.
taylor: I can flip routing for heatmap to strict-affinity and patch the canary; should be low risk.
infra-bot: Routing config change submitted: https://infra/changes/5681 — awaiting approval from @oncall.
jamie: also want a new dashboard tile: "heatmap cold-load cost" that shows combined parse+eval+kv-miss penalty by route and by deployment. will help catch regressions earlier.
oana: add an alert too: heatmap combined-penalty p95 > 300ms for >5m.
rui: longer term: we need per-route splitpoint priority and per-route kvcache TTL. current global knobs are too coarse.
taylor: agreed — we should add metadata to route manifests: {"splitpointPriority": "inline|lazy", "kvcacheTTL": ms}. small infra change.
jamie: also can we add a tiny prefetch for the heatmap worker (prefetch link rel=preload) to reduce parse stalls? would be a low-risk perf win.
oana: yes, but only for routes that we mark high-LCP. we'll include that in the per-route policy.
jamie: OK plan: 
1) taylor flips routing to strict-affinity (in flight).
2) infra-bot will apply a hold for the shared-visuals rollback if routing flip doesn't improve in 10m.
3) oana to add dashboard tile + alert.
4) rui to scope per-route TTL/priority change for next sprint.
5) jamie to propose small preload for heatmap worker in the rollout checklist.

taylor: routing flip complete: https://infra/changes/5681/status — propagated to all regions. monitoring now.
jamie: monitoring shows heatmap p95 dropped from 460ms -> 210ms after routing flip. kvcache misses still a bit elevated but much better.
oana: putting dashboard + alert ticket: https://tasks/RED-1212 — will triage today.
rui: I'll start a spike for per-route TTL and attach a prototype to the ticket.
jamie: nice work. let's not forget to update rollout docs: "when splitting chunks, consider per-route priority and test kvcache TTL impact in canary".
taylor: adding note to the canary checklist now.
infra-bot: Change 5681 closed.
jamie: thanks everyone. will watch the alerts for the hour and then decide whether to rollback shared-visuals or continue with per-route fixes.
